title: Calibration job orchestration: artifact indexing, TTL curation, and ACLs for FP8/INT8 sweeps
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement: Calibration campaigns (FP8/INT8 sweeps and nested hyperparameter sweeps) currently produce many ephemeral artifacts (prefix caches, per-run checkpoints, eval traces, quant profile candidates). Without a coherent orchestration layer in the Console we face three operational issues: 1) noisy artifact stores that increase storage costs and surface area for data governance, 2) difficulty auditing which artifacts correspond to validated, promoted quant profiles, and 3) unclear RBAC and promotion semantics for multi-tenant teams running shared calibration pipelines.

Goal: Deliver orchestration controls in Redwood Console that index calibration runs and artifacts, apply TTL-based curation policies, provide fine-grained ACLs for run-level artifacts, and surface an accuracy-validation gating workflow that explicitly ties artifacts to promoted quant profiles. The feature should support both FP8 and INT8 calibration campaigns and preserve lineage for compliance/rollback.

Scope in this ticket: design and implement the Console UI flows and backend metadata index for: run registration (name, model, dataset, seed, param sweep), artifact tagging and searchable indexing, per-run TTL and retention classes (ephemeral, staging, canonical), ACLs at run and artifact granularity, promotion flow from staged artifacts to canonical quant profiles with validation gates, and an automated archival/GC job that emits audit events. Backend changes (ENG deps) include adding lightweight indexing tables, ACL checks on artifact read/promote/delete, and hooks to the accuracy-eval service to gate promotions. Excluded: full storage tiering migration and cold-storage export (future tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: can create a calibration run and choose retention class (ephemeral/staging/canonical)
Runs and artifacts are indexed and searchable by run id, model name, quant target (FP8/INT8), and tags
Owner can set per-run TTL and override at artifact type level (e.g., keep eval-traces for 90 days, checkpoints for 7 days)
ACLs enforced: team members with 'viewer' role cannot promote or delete canonical artifacts; 'operator' role can promote staging->canonical
Promotion gate requires a passing accuracy validation result linked to the artifact before changing status to canonical
GC job respects TTLs and emits audit log entries for deletions; deleted artifacts are soft-deleted for 7 days before physical purge
Audit trail records lineage: which run produced artifact, which evaluation snapshot validated it, and which user triggered promotion/delete
tasks: Design Console components: run creation modal, retention/TTL controls, promotion dialog, artifact index table
Define metadata schema for index: run_id, model, quant_target, tags, artifact_types, created_at, ttl, owner, status, lineage_refs
Spec ACL matrix and map to RBAC roles used by Private/Dedicated customers
Wire accuracy-eval API: add 'validation_status' to artifact metadata and block promotion if failing
Implement backend index and TTL worker (ENG to own)
Add audit event hooks for promote/delete/GC
Add unit and e2e tests for promotion gating and ACL enforcement
Create copy/content for in-console help and admin doc

notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping TTL defaults conservative (30d staging, 7d ephemeral) to avoid accidental data loss vs. storage costs. We opted for shorter ephemerals and explicit retention overrides per-run. For multi-tenant Private deployments we will surface tenant-level policy enforcements in a follow-up. Need to align with legal on audit retention for regulated customers.
